reason: Moses is prominently portrayed as the national representative and de facto leader of the Israelite people. Throughout this passage, he serves as: (1) the sole spokesperson for Israel before Pharaoh, delivering God's demands to 'let my people go' (וְאַחַר בָּאוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה); (2) the negotiator of Israel's freedom, directly engaging with Pharaoh on terms of departure; (3) the intermediary between God and the nation, receiving divine commands and executing them on behalf of his people; and (4) the recognized leader figure to whom Pharaoh addresses his responses and commands. While his authority is derived from his prophetic relationship with God rather than secular political appointment, he exercises undisputed leadership over the nation during this critical moment of liberation. He negotiates, intercedes, and speaks with complete authority as the people's leader.
